result.title: SIRNET: Causal Adaptation of Pretrained Embeddings for Semiparametric Treatment-Effect Estimation Under Surrogacy
result.summary: Modern experiments increasingly produce rich post-treatment objects---such as text, images, and video---that may provide early surrogate signals for outcomes that are delayed, expensive, or observed only for a subset of participants. A pretrained encoder can turn such an object into a strong generic embedding, but the embedding is not trained for the estimation tasks required by a causal estimator and may emphasize information irrelevant to the causal target. We propose SIRNET, a Surrogate-Informed Representation adaptation framework for neural-NETwork-based causal estimation in the presence of unstructured post-treatment surrogates. Starting from pretrained surrogate embeddings, SIRNET learns a shared adapter jointly for outcome prediction, treatment propensity, and arm-specific surrogate marginalization, beyond the generic pretraining objective. The resulting covariate and surrogate representations provide a common interface for these nuisance tasks. The final treatment-effect estimate and confidence interval are obtained from cross-fitted orthogonal scores that attain the semiparametric efficiency bound under the stated nuisance-rate conditions. We also validate SIRNET's performance in synthetic and semisynthetic experiments, as well as the Anti-Amyloid in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease (A4) trial, using frozen pretrained brain-MRI embeddings as surrogates for a long-term outcome.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SIRNET，在存在处理后非结构化替代变量（文本、图像、视频等）时，从预训练编码器嵌入出发，通过共享 adapter 联合学习结果预测、处理倾向与分臂替代变量边缘化，再用交叉拟合的正交得分给出半参数有效的处理效应估计与置信区间，并在合成、半合成实验与 A4 脑 MRI 试验上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作指出通用预训练嵌入可能强调与目标无关的信息，需针对下游目标改造表示——这可作为「任务必要信息是否保留在内部状态」这一问题表述的远域类比，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理状态生成或视觉证据筛选，借鉴价值需较多核查。
